name: Grommash Hellscream
summary: After the Third War, Grommash Hellscream's people are free of the Blood Curse. Once bound to the Burning Legion by his thirst for battle, the Warsong chieftain gave his life to slay Mannoroth in Ashenvale and free the orcs.

sections.title: The First Drink and the Iron Will
sections.body: Before the Dark Portal opened, Grom Hellscream led the Warsong clan with fierce resolve. His pitch-black tattooed jaw and the deadly sweep of his two-handed axe, Gorehowl, set him apart. On Draenor, Gul'dan and the Shadow Council offered the orcs demonic strength. Grom was the first chieftain to drink the blood of the pit lord Mannoroth. The draught bound the orcs to demonic service and filled them with burning bloodlust. Many chieftains perished or lost themselves to it, but Grom kept his fierce spirit through the old Horde's horrors. He carried a quiet ache for what his people had surrendered.

sections.title: A Brotherhood in the Wilds
sections.body: Left behind on Draenor during the Second War, Grom later crossed the Dark Portal and was stranded when the rift was shattered. For nearly fifteen years, he and the surviving Warsong warriors evaded the Alliance of Lordaeron. They endured the lethargy and despair that followed the fading of the demon blood. Then a young fugitive named Thrall found Grom in the wilderness, and hope returned. Grom saw Thrall's strength and noble heart, and taught him the proud heritage of their people. Together with Orgrim Doomhammer, they rallied the scattered clans, broke open the human internment camps, and began the New Horde.

sections.title: Fall and Final Redemption
sections.body: During the Third War, Grom's aggression rose again in Ashenvale's ancient forests. The night elves and the demigod Cenarius pressed his clan hard, and Grom drank from a fountain corrupted with Mannoroth's blood to save them. Bound again to the demon lord, he turned against his own people. Thrall and Jaina Proudmoore captured him and cleansed his spirit with ancient shamanic and arcane rites. Restored to his senses and burdened with guilt, Grom pursued Mannoroth into Demon Fall Canyon. He drove Gorehowl into the demon lord's chest, ending the demonic curse forever. Hellfire took Grom's life.

faq.answer: Grommash Hellscream, known as Grom, led the Warsong clan and served as Thrall's trusted lieutenant. Famous for Gorehowl, he was also the first orc to drink Mannoroth's blood and accept the demonic pact. He redeemed his legacy by slaying Mannoroth in Kalimdor and freeing the orcs from the Blood Curse.

Grom died in Demon Fall Canyon in Ashenvale, where he faced the pit lord Mannoroth. He leapt into the air and cleaved the demon's chest with Gorehowl, shattering its heart. The burst of demonic hellfire fatally wounded Grom, who died declaring that he had freed himself and his people.

faq.q: What is Grom's connection to Thrall?
faq.answer: Grom was the first clan chieftain Thrall met after escaping the internment camp of Durnholde. He took the young orc under his wing, teaching him orcish traditions, language, and culture. Thrall saw Grom as an older brother and spiritual guide, while Grom saw Thrall as the visionary who could lead their shattered race back to honor.

faq.q: Why was Grom's jaw tattooed black?
faq.answer: Grom's lower jaw bore a solid black tattoo that set him apart among the orcish chieftains and made him easy to recognize in battle. The tales told of him do not record what the mark meant.

faq.q: Why did Grom drink demon blood a second time?
faq.answer: Grom drank demon blood again to save his clan after night elves and the demigod Cenarius decimated it while it harvested lumber in Ashenvale. Cenarius was nearly invincible against mortal weapons. Grom found a pool corrupted by Mannoroth's blood and drank, knowing the dreadful cost, to gain the demonic fury to defeat him.

Grom rests in Demon Fall Canyon in southeastern Ashenvale, where he struck down Mannoroth. A stone monument marks his burial site, with an epitaph by Thrall honoring Grom's courage and ultimate sacrifice for the Horde.

angles.text: As an orc, you revere Grommash as your people's savior. His sacrifice in Ashenvale broke the demonic Blood Curse that held the orcs for generations, allowing the New Horde to live with pride and free will.
As a member of the Horde, you remember Grom as a fierce warrior whose reckless temper led his people into darkness. His unyielding courage bought their survival and freedom in Kalimdor.
As a night elf, you may remember Grom with bitterness: he invaded Ashenvale in a demonic frenzy, defiled its sacred groves, and killed the demigod Cenarius.
As a warrior, you can study Grom's battlefield prowess and mastery of Gorehowl. His story shows the cost of unchecked rage and the force of an indomitable fighting spirit.
